correctness.rationale: There is one zero word and every offset of an isolated one occurs; all n weight-one words have the same image. For a factor with at least two ones, the second one is at offset r+2^j where j is the first marker index and r is the first-one offset. Excluding the preceding marker gives 0≤r<2^(j−1) when j≥1, while j=0 forces r=0 by the one-sided boundary. The word is fixed by (j,r). The image's first one is at offset r+2^j−1 by the one-step stack rule: the leading zeros and the first internal zero block are emitted before the first one is popped. Its allowable offset intervals [2^j−1, 3·2^(j−1)−2] for j≥1 and {0} for j=0 are disjoint. Thus the image recovers (j,r), and weight preservation separates all three classes. For n≥2 and k=floor(log₂n), j<k contributes 2^(k−1) factors including j=0; j=k contributes min(2^(k−1),n−2^k); larger j contribute none. This gives M(n), including dyadic endpoints, hence the stated counts and difference. For n=1 both letters are fixed. A separate literal-stack simulation on complete finite window sets corroborated every length 1 through 256 (`cd /workspace && python3 power_marker_reproduction.py`); the interval argument, not that simulation, establishes the all-length claim.
